paras: The killing of Dennis Brothen took place on the night of June 1, 1881, when a party of four young white men came to the home of Brothen, a Black man, in Camp County, Texas, near Jefferson, and two of them killed him. Brothen had fired on the party, killing Calvin Cope and mortally wounding Israel Hagrand, and the two unhurt men escaped. A brief dispatch from Jefferson carried the story to papers from West Virginia to California and Montana within a week.

According to the dispatch datelined Jefferson, June 2, the four young men "visited the residence" of Brothen, described as "colored," the night before. No paper stated why they went there, although weekly digests later said they had "attacked a colored man's house" or "meddled with the cabin." Brothen "fired into them," shooting Calvin Cope dead and mortally wounding Israel Hagrand. The two other men then "killed the negro and escaped"; how he was killed was not reported.
No report of an arrest, inquest or prosecution of the two men appears in the coverage, nor any later word on whether Hagrand died of his wound.

The item ran on June 3 in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer under the head "Texas Tragedies," beside a report of convicts killed in an escape near Sealy, and in the Cheyenne Daily Leader and the Sacramento Daily Record-Union. On June 4 the Salt Lake Herald placed it in "The Criminal Calendar" and the Daily Los Angeles Herald printed it with a June 3 dateline; the Weekly Miner of Butte, Montana, followed on June 7. Each wire copy called Brothen "colored" and "the negro," named the two white casualties, and left the killers unnamed and their purpose unexplained.

Weekly papers in Wisconsin and Minnesota reworded the story on June 8. The "Tragical Tales" digest in the Watertown Republican and Mower County Transcript had the men "meddled with the cabin," and the St. Paul Daily Globe had already said they "attacked" the house. The New Ulm Weekly Review dropped the word "white" and named the householder "Dennis Young." No Black newspaper coverage of the killing was found.

The papers spelled the dead man's surname Brothen, Brotemni and Broteuni, and the wounded man's Hagrand, Lagunde and La Grande, variants of a single telegraphed dispatch. Most copies called the four men "white," while shortened versions said only "four young men."

accounts.label: Jefferson wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Four young white men visited the residence of Dennis Brothen, colored, who fired into them, killing Calvin Cope and mortally wounding Israel Hagrand; the other two killed him and escaped.

accounts.label: Weekly digest (St. Paul and 'Tragical Tales')
accounts.gist: Recast the visit as an attack: the four men 'attacked a colored man's house' or 'meddled with the cabin' before he opened fire.

framing.detail: Ran the Jefferson dispatch unchanged under crime-roundup heads such as 'Texas Tragedies' and 'The Criminal Calendar', calling Brothen 'colored' and 'the negro' and giving no reason for the visit.
Weekly digests rewrote the visit as the men having 'attacked' the house or 'meddled with the cabin', without comment.

conflicts.note: Probably OCR and telegraphic variants of one name, except 'Young' in the New Ulm rewrite; the true spelling cannot be settled from these texts.
Versions that omit 'white' are shortened copies of the same wire; none says the men were anything but white.
The digest wordings are rewrites of the wire, not independent reports; the purpose of the visit is never stated.

record_check.dossier: The Black victim is Dennis Brothen alone; Calvin Cope (killed) and Israel Hagrand (wounded) were members of the attacking party, shot by Brothen
Four young white men, of whom two unnamed survivors killed Brothen; Cope and Hagrand were the other two
A party (band) of four young men, not a crowd
Jefferson is the dateline; the shooting was in Camp County 'near Jefferson'
